West Virginia home loans

Purchase and refinance loans for homes in West Virginia.

Who you'll work with

Ibex isn't licensed in West Virginia, so we don't make loans here. When you request a quote for a West Virginia property, we refer you to an independent mortgage lender licensed in West Virginia. That lender sets your rate and terms and handles your loan. We may receive a referral fee, which doesn't change what you pay.

Buying a home in West Virginia

Get pre-qualified before you shop so you know your price range and can make a strong offer. First-time buyers in West Virginia can often combine an FHA or conventional loan with state or local down payment assistance. Veterans should look at VA loans, and buyers outside major metro areas may qualify for USDA zero-down financing.

Refinancing in West Virginia

A refinance can lower your payment, remove mortgage insurance or turn equity into cash. Compare closing costs with your monthly savings to see how long it takes to break even.

Investing in West Virginia rentals

DSCR loans let investors qualify on a property's rent instead of personal income.

West Virginia questions

What home loans are available in West Virginia?

Conventional, FHA, VA, USDA (in eligible areas), jumbo, renovation and investor DSCR loans are all used in West Virginia. Which one fits depends on your credit, down payment and the property.

Is there down payment assistance in West Virginia?

West Virginia's housing finance agency and many local governments offer down payment and closing cost help for qualifying buyers. Programs open and close often, so ask when you apply.

What if I'm behind on my mortgage in West Virginia?

Contact your servicer right away and ask about a loan modification or forbearance. Free HUD-approved housing counselors serve West Virginia at 800-569-4287. See our guide for homeowners behind on payments.
